newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end higher, Olivetti soars.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end higher, Olivetti soars.

text.p: Italian shares closed mostly higher on Tuesday, hauled up by a sharp recovery in Olivetti and a boom in speculative trading of Stet and Telecom Italia savings shares.
Montedison also advanced, closing 1.98 percent higher at 1,083 lire, boosted by the influx of cash into the company's coffers after a large number of investors converted warrants into company stock.
Stock traders said the likelihood of Montedison paying a dividend wqas believed to have been increased by the conversion and shares in Compart also rose 3.98 percent in sympathy.

Fiat shares, which jumped last week after the announcement of a government incentive scheme to kick-start domestic car sales, were off as investors reassessed the likely impact of the initiative on the group's bottom line.
Fiat ordinary shares finished 2.85 percent lower at 4,255 lire. The all-share Mibtel index was 0.18 percent higher at 10,592 with the blue-chip Mib30 index gaining 0.06 percent to finish at 15,724.

Olivetti was the star performer of the session, rising 7.35 percent to end the day at 587.3 lire on news that the company could be close to selling its troubled PC division to a the U.S.-owned Centenary Group.
The chairman of white group company Zanussi, Gianmario Rossignolo, is also involved in the Centenary bid.

Share buying in Stet and Telecom Italia savings shares was prompted by expectations that investors may be given the option to switch their shares into ordinary stock when the two companies are merged.
